mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined for two consecutive weeks (24.0 -> 20.1 -> 13.6), indicating people are spending less time at home and resuming out-of-home activity. This continued decline in RESIDENTIAL mechanically frees time for shopping and leisure trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.0 to 13.6 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in TRANSIT mobility beyond a 15-point weekly gain signals renewed use of public transport for commuting and errands, which in turn drives incidental retail and recreation visits along transit routes, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -60.4 to -50.4 between t-1w and t-0w, a 10-point gain nearing the threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of a TRANSIT weekly gain exceeding 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reinforces a broader return-to-commute pattern: workplace reopening increases transit demand, and the two together generate compounded retail footfall gains greater than either series alone would predict, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved each of the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than the sum of growth predicted by WORKPLACES and TRANSIT individually, indicating no interaction effect, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint recovery in both series.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden large jump in PARKS mobility (from -38.4 to -24.9, a 13.5-point gain) indicates a loosening of outdoor activity restrictions by local authorities. This policy relaxation signal typically precedes broader reopening of retail establishments, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points in the latest week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -38.4 at t-1w to -24.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week following a PARKS weekly gain exceeding 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has steadily recovered from a trough of -24.3 toward -13.4, reflecting normalization of essential-goods shopping routines as a seasonal/behavioral baseline stabilizes. This steady recovery in essential retail typically leads broader retail-and-recreation recovery over a four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved each week from -24.3 to -13.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to trend upward over the next 28 days despite three or more consecutive weeks of GROCERY_PHARM improvement.

mechanism_narrative: Once RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below the +15 point threshold, it signals that time-at-home has normalized close to a pre-crisis baseline, freeing discretionary time for retail and recreation trips, which increases RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to 13.6 at t-0w, crossing below the 15-point threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of RESIDENTIAL dropping below 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in WORKPLACES mobility and decreases in RESIDENTIAL mobility jointly indicate a coordinated policy-driven reopening of economic activity. The interaction of these two signals produces a stronger retail rebound than either alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -46.6 to -27.6 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 20.1 to 13.6 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES continues rising and RESIDENTIAL continues falling in tandem.

mechanism_narrative: If both PARKS and TRANSIT weekly changes decelerate to under 5 points, indicating a plateau in outdoor and transit activity recovery, this signals a stabilization regime in which RETAIL_REC growth also stalls or reverses slightly over the next week, as the broad reopening momentum has exhausted its short-term drivers.
candidate_trigger: both PARKS and TRANSIT week-on-week change fall below 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and PARKS both showed large recent swings that could decelerate
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next week even when both PARKS and TRANSIT weekly changes fall below 5 points, indicating no plateau effect.
